Welcome, and thank you for signing up to test MailCraft.

**Getting started**
- Install the [latest release](https://github.com/UCS-Care-Group/mailcraft/releases/latest). The builds aren't signed yet, so Windows and macOS will warn you the first time you open them.
- For a work or school account, your organisation may need to approve MailCraft once ("Need admin approval"). MailCraft says what to do: open Microsoft's approval page if you're an administrator, or copy a message for one.
- Keep Outlook or Outlook on the web to hand. Moves, deletions and read marks go to your server, and beta builds can still get things wrong.

**Reporting**
- One problem per issue, through the [problem form](https://github.com/UCS-Care-Group/mailcraft/issues/new?template=problem.yml). Mention this issue so it's linked to you.
- Say which version you're on (File › About MailCraft) and whether it lost anything, crashed, or disagrees with Outlook on the web. Those get the `data-loss`, `crash` and `out-of-step` labels and are fixed first.
- From the release after 0.3.0, paste **Help › Copy Diagnostics** into the report: it has the version, the platform and the end of the log, with addresses, names and paths taken out.
- From the release after 0.6.0, **Report a Problem** (in the title bar, and in Help) starts the report for you, two ways. *Open on GitHub* fills in the problem form in your browser and saves the diagnostics to a file you attach there by drag and drop; the issue is public and needs a GitHub account. *Send by Email* starts a new message to the maintainers in MailCraft, from your own account, with the diagnostics attached; it stays private. Either way you check it and send it yourself: MailCraft sends nothing.
- Put nothing private in an issue: no message content, addresses or organisation names.

**This issue is your log.** A short comment once a week is plenty: which devices you used, roughly how many days, and anything odd that didn't merit its own issue.

**The beta run** counts 14 working days (Monday to Friday, about three weeks) on at least 2 devices, on a Microsoft account. It is under way: say here when you start, and your 14 working days count from then. Use it as much or as little as you like before that.

**Credit.** Once you've tested a release, you can be credited by name in About › Testers, if you ticked the box above (or say so in this issue).

New releases are announced in #11. **Watch → Custom → Releases** on the repository gets you a notification.

Thanks again! A maintainer will add you to the roster in #11.

<sub>This reply is posted automatically for every tester sign-up.</sub>
